title: I made my first game with AI assistance. How does it look, and what would you improve?
author: Beautiful_Ad9914
selftext:
Hi everyone! *Seashell Hoarder* is the first video game I’ve made. I started learning PC game development as a hobby about four or five months ago; my main background is in board game design.

I hope to build a much larger digital board game someday. Before taking that on, I wanted to make a smaller game and learn what AI-assisted development is actually like. I’ve used Blender MCP, GPT, and Claude during development.

The game is about exploring a beach, finding seashells, cleaning them, and organizing a growing collection. Its Steam page is live, but the game and demo haven’t been released yet.

I’d appreciate honest feedback on what I’m showing so far:

* Does the game’s visual style appeal to you? What would you change?
* Can you tell what you would do in the game from the footage and Steam page?
* Is there anything that looks confusing or needs more polish?

Steam page: \[store.steampowered.com/app/5314120/Seashell\_Hoarder\]

comments.author: Content_Mind_196
comments.body:
It looks really good! How much AI did you use, and what model did you use?

Notice the game is stylized to a specific theme, did you ask for that specifically, the low poly aspect?

replies.author: Beautiful_Ad9914
replies.body: Thank you. I developed it in Unity with not much knowledge first but I am used to it now. I like low poly and game category is collecthaton/organizing game.

comments.author: Imnotanad
comments.body: I like it. I would change the shelfs to darkish wood and vary a little bit the general color of assets ( not the shells. The shells are OK ) like walls and a clear sky. But that's personal! The game is fine

replies.author: Beautiful_Ad9914
replies.body: Thanks! I will give it a consideration.

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body: Are those the real shell names? Do you usually find all those shells at the same beach?

replies.author: Beautiful_Ad9914
replies.body: Yes real shell names I have found in the internet. All shells on the ground(some of them  can only be claimed with tools) and you just organize them.

replies.author: Seven-Prime
replies.body:
Not my type of game, but I know lots of people enjoy this type.

I ask about the shell names and locations as an interesting use of AI. Like you find different shells in the Caribbean vs Mediterranean. Having the ai do the research to figure it out and classify them into regions (levels). Anyways, just a thought.

Looks good!

comments.author: KrerdlyBeloved
comments.body: The music, for sure, it has the same musical 'style' that a lot of other Claude creations will go with. You'll want to give it more libraries to work with, or have some original music/sound made for it.

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: It bothers me that the shells don't go directly into the basket on the beach scene or come directly out of the basket on the shelving scene.
